IPv4 route table and lookup logic with /32 hashmap support, clear, and formatted printing.

# Purpose
`fd_fib4.c` implements the IPv4 forwarding information base type `fd_fib4_t`. It provides the core life-cycle functions for the table, including [`fd_fib4_align`](<#fd_fib4_align>), [`fd_fib4_footprint`](<#fd_fib4_footprint>), [`fd_fib4_new`](<#fd_fib4_new>), [`fd_fib4_join`](<#fd_fib4_join>), [`fd_fib4_leave`](<#fd_fib4_leave>), [`fd_fib4_delete`](<#fd_fib4_delete>), and [`fd_fib4_clear`](<#fd_fib4_clear>). The file also exposes accessors such as [`fd_fib4_max`](<#fd_fib4_max>), [`fd_fib4_peer_max`](<#fd_fib4_peer_max>), and [`fd_fib4_cnt`](<#fd_fib4_cnt>). The data structure stores a route table and a separate hash map for `/32` host routes. The [`fd_fib4_new`](<#fd_fib4_new>) function lays out all internal storage in one memory region and initializes the default route entry.

The file also implements route insertion and lookup. [`fd_fib4_insert`](<#fd_fib4_insert>) adds routes to the main table or to the hash map for host routes, and it uses a generation counter to detect concurrent updates. [`fd_fib4_lookup`](<#fd_fib4_lookup>) searches the hash map first, then scans the route table to select the best match by prefix length and metric. If it detects a torn read or another error, it returns a blackhole hop. When `FD_HAS_HOSTED` is set, the file also includes [`fd_fib4_fprintf`](<#fd_fib4_fprintf>) and helper code to print the route table and hash map entries in a human-readable form.
